All individuals with atopic dermatitis showed attenuated clinical responses compared to controls, but responses were still present.

evidence.experimental_conditions: primary immunization with DNCB while on cyclophosphamide; retest with 100 µg DNCB after 9 months of cyclophosphamide therapy; human patients with rheumatoid arthritis
evidence.support_text: In patients on cyclophosphamide, induction of primary immunization with DNCB was markedly inhibited: of 11 patients, minimal skin sensitization was induced in only 1, whereas marked sensitization invariably occurred in all 11 placebo patients. At retesting after 18 months, all except 1 patient who had received cyclophosphamide at the time of primary immunization remained unresponsive to 100 µg DNCB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: primary immunization with DNCB; retest with 100 µg DNCB after 9 months; human patients with rheumatoid arthritis on placebo
evidence.support_text: In the placebo group, marked sensitization to DNCB invariably occurred in all 11 patients. In contrast, only 1 of 11 patients on cyclophosphamide developed minimal sensitization. Retesting with 100 µg DNCB confirmed these results: strongly positive tests in placebo-immunized patients, and unresponsiveness in cyclophosphamide-treated patients.

evidence.support_text: KGL, Inc evaluated the contact-sensitizing potential of a mousse (concentrate) containing 1.72% active capryl/capramidopropyl betaine in a maximization study with 26 participants. Induction involved SLS pretreatment followed by occluded test material for 48 h, up to 5 exposures; challenge after 10-day rest with 5% SLS for 1 h then test material occluded for 48 h. No adverse or unexpected reactions occurred, no contact allergy recorded. It was concluded that the mousse containing 1.72% capryl/capramidopropyl betaine did not have a detectable contact-sensitizing potential and was not likely to cause contact sensitivity reactions under normal use conditions. Estimated dose/unit area = 4.9×10² µg/cm².
